script.source: #!/bin/sh C=$(cat /proc/cmdline) zget() { echo "$C" | tr ' ' '\n' | sed -n "s/^$1=//p" | head -n1; } H=$(zget fluxhost); [ -n "$H" ] || H=fluxserver HS=$(echo "$H" | sed 's/[\/&]/\\&/g') # fluxpass is deliberately not substituted in: AutoYaST caches this profile # onto the installed system, so the password is set by the chroot-script. cp /tmp/profile/autoinst.xml /tmp/profile/modified.xml sed -i "s/@ZH@/$HS/g" /tmp/profile/modified.xml

#!/bin/sh # AutoYaST traces every line of this script into # /var/adm/autoinstall/logs/<name>.log with set -x - variable assignments # included - so tracing must go dark before the password is ever read, or # the plaintext lands in an archived log flux-scrub's fluxpass= pattern # does not match (observed: "+ P=<the password>" in the log). set +x # Credentials are set HERE, in a chroot-script, and deliberately not in a # post-script. AutoYaST's own documentation is explicit about the difference: # chroot-scripts run "before the machine reboots for the first time", while # post-scripts run "after it has booted the system for the first time". In a # post-script /proc/cmdline is therefore the INSTALLED system's command line, # which carries no fluxpass= - so reading it there finds nothing, both # accounts keep the locked "!" hash from the <users> section below, and every # automated install finishes as an unreachable box. # # No fallback password: a missing fluxpass= leaves both accounts locked rather # than handing out a default that is published in a public repo. P=$(tr ' ' '\n' < /proc/cmdline | sed -n 's/^fluxpass=//p' | head -n1) if [ -n "$P" ]; then # NOT plain chpasswd: SUSE routes it through PAM's quality stack even # for root, and a password cracklib dislikes is REJECTED - "BAD # PASSWORD: it is based on a dictionary word" in the script log, both # accounts still locked, and the box installs perfectly unreachable # (found by the install matrix). The operator's password is not this # installer's to veto: hash it here and hand chpasswd the finished # hash with -e, which skips the quality check. perl is part of # inst-sys (YaST depends on it); the password reaches it through the # ENVIRONMENT, never argv - same pattern, same reasoning, as # src/pve-bashrc. Refuse a non-SHA-512 result rather than shipping # whatever a fallback crypt() produced. HASH=$(FLUXP="$P" perl -e ' my @c = ("a".."z", "A".."Z", "0".."9", ".", "/"); my $s = join "", map { $c[rand @c] } 1..16; print crypt($ENV{FLUXP}, "\$6\$$s\$");') || HASH= case $HASH in '$6$'*) # Deferred to FIRST BOOT, not applied here: at chroot-script time # the 'user' account does not exist yet (YaST materialises the # <users> section afterwards), and SUSE's chpasswd is all-or- # nothing - the whole batch is rejected, root included ("user # 'user' does not exist ... changes ignored", verbatim in this # script's own archived log). And whatever YaST writes afterwards # would overwrite anything set now. So the HASH - never the # password - is parked root-only on the target and applied by a # oneshot at first boot, ordered Before=sshd: after every YaST # stage has finished writing accounts, before the box is ever # reachable. The oneshot deletes the file and itself; the same # hash lives in /etc/shadow from that moment on, so the file at # rest adds no exposure shadow does not already carry. umask 077 printf '%s\n' "$HASH" > /mnt/etc/flux-cred.hash mkdir -p /mnt/usr/local/sbin cat > /mnt/usr/local/sbin/flux-cred <<'FLUXEOF' #!/bin/sh H=$(cat /etc/flux-cred.hash 2>/dev/null) if [ -n "$H" ]; then getent passwd user >/dev/null 2>&1 || useradd -m -c 'Default User' user printf 'root:%s\nuser:%s\n' "$H" "$H" | chpasswd -e \ || echo "FLUX: first-boot chpasswd -e failed - accounts stay LOCKED." >&2 fi rm -f /etc/flux-cred.hash systemctl disable flux-cred.service >/dev/null 2>&1 || : rm -f /etc/systemd/system/flux-cred.service /usr/local/sbin/flux-cred FLUXEOF chmod 700 /mnt/usr/local/sbin/flux-cred cat > /mnt/etc/systemd/system/flux-cred.service <<'FLUXEOF' [Unit] Description=FluxBilling: apply install-time credentials DefaultDependencies=no After=local-fs.target Before=sshd.service
[Service] Type=oneshot ExecStart=/usr/local/sbin/flux-cred
[Install] WantedBy=multi-user.target FLUXEOF chroot /mnt systemctl enable flux-cred.service ;; *) echo "FLUX: crypt() did not produce a SHA-512 hash - root and user stay LOCKED." >&2 ;; esac else echo "FLUX: no fluxpass= on the kernel command line - root and user stay LOCKED." >&2 fi unset P HASH
sed -i 's/^#\?PermitRootLogin.*/PermitRootLogin yes/' /mnt/etc/ssh/sshd_config
# YaST copies its logs and the cached profile onto the target at the very end # of the run - after this script - so the redaction cannot happen here. Install # the same first-boot oneshot the other families use, ordered ahead of sshd so # the box is never reachable while the password is still in the logs. mkdir -p /mnt/usr/local/sbin cat > /mnt/usr/local/sbin/flux-scrub <<'FLUXEOF' #!/bin/sh for d in /var/log/YaST2 /var/adm/autoinstall /var/log/installer; do [ -d "$d" ] || continue find "$d" -type f 2>/dev/null | while read -r f; do sed -i 's/fluxpass=[^[:space:]]*/fluxpass=<redacted>/g' "$f" 2>/dev/null || : done done systemctl disable flux-scrub.service >/dev/null 2>&1 || : rm -f /etc/systemd/system/flux-scrub.service /usr/local/sbin/flux-scrub FLUXEOF chmod 700 /mnt/usr/local/sbin/flux-scrub cat > /mnt/etc/systemd/system/flux-scrub.service <<'FLUXEOF' [Unit] Description=FluxBilling: strip install-time credentials from installer logs DefaultDependencies=no After=local-fs.target Before=sshd.service
[Service] Type=oneshot ExecStart=/usr/local/sbin/flux-scrub
[Install] WantedBy=multi-user.target FLUXEOF chroot /mnt systemctl enable flux-scrub.service
